# commentary/

## Purpose
Generated commentary on a report pack, held as a DRAFT until a named person approves it. Table `report_commentary`, migrations 611 and 612.

## Caller contract
Called by `pages/api/accounting/commentary/*` under `withAuth`; company always from the session. Consumed on the public side by `share/sharedPackService.ts`, which selects `approved_text` and filters `status = 'approved'`. Every statement here carries `company_id`, including the UPDATEs.

## Main signatures
- `listCommentary(companyId, params) → CommentaryRow[]` — the whole pack, unfiltered. There is no section parameter on the route or the hook; `CommentaryBlock` owns the per-section filter.
- `generateDrafts({ companyId, userId, params, data, replace? }) → { written, skipped }`.
- `approveCommentary(companyId, id, userId, editedText?)` / `rejectCommentary(...)` → `CommentaryResult`, failing with `not_found` (404), `empty_draft` (400), `invalid_text` (400), `text_too_long` (400), `commentary_budget_exceeded` (400) or `invalid_state` (409) — the route must not collapse them. `editedText` absent copies `draft_text`; present writes the trimmed text and leaves `draft_text` the machine draft.
- `MAX_APPROVED_PACK_EMS`, `MAX_UNBUDGETED_CHARS`, `commentaryEms`, `packEmsUsed`, `approxCharsLeft`, `normaliseEditedText`, `editedTextProblem` (`commentaryLimits.ts`, client-safe) — the ONE cost function the service, the editor and the tests share. `commentaryBudget.ts` holds the server half (which packs are budgeted, the per-pack lock, the sum).
- `nextStatus(current, action) → Transition`; `buildDraftSentences(data) → DraftSentence[]`; `buildManagementPackData(companyId, params)`.

## Business rules
- **Status machine** (`commentaryState.ts` is the only place a status changes): `draft → approved` (approve), `draft → rejected` (reject), `* → draft` (generate). `generate` on an approved row FAILS.
- **The `replace` gate.** `replace: true` is the only path that re-drafts a row a person already ruled on: it withdraws an approval and revives a rejection. Without it both are left alone and reported in `skipped` — a discarded sentence does not come back because somebody pressed Generate again. The route restricts `replace` to owner/admin; `CommentaryPanel` puts an explicit, single-use confirmation in front of it.
- A withdrawal is STAMPED, not erased: `withdrawn_by`/`withdrawn_at` are set and `approved_text`/`approved_by`/`approved_at` survive, so the row still says who signed off. Nothing leaks — the published query filters on status.
- The `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... WHERE` repeats the decision at the write, on the row's state at write time, because another session can approve or reject inside the read-to-write window.
- An empty or whitespace-only draft is never approvable. The 611 CHECK would store the blank.
- Approval writes status, text, approver and timestamp in ONE statement so the CHECK never sees a half-approved row; the WHERE repeats the guard so two racing approvals cannot both write.
- The draft builder never writes `approved_text`. Nothing generated reaches a share link without a person.

## Recent changes
- 2026-10-07: approve-with-edits. `POST .../[id]/approve` takes an optional `{ text: string }`; the body must be absent/empty or a plain object (a string or array is a 400, never read as 'no text'), and `text` must be a string, never coerced. An edit writes the trimmed text and leaves `draft_text` the machine draft; CRLF and lone CR are normalised to LF before validating and storing; text with no visible character (whitespace, `\p{Cf}`, Hangul fillers, the braille blank, Khmer inherent vowels, CGJ, variation selectors) is `empty_draft`; NUL/C0 controls/lone surrogates are `invalid_text`. A pack with no fixed page (management, monthly) caps an EDITED row at `MAX_UNBUDGETED_CHARS = 4000` (`text_too_long`). A PLAIN approval is a compare-and-set on the draft it costed (`AND draft_text = <read>`): a regenerate committing in between gives `invalid_state` 'draft text changed, reload'. **Budget:** approved text of a BOARD pack is held to `MAX_APPROVED_PACK_EMS = 560`, costed with the page's own ruler (`packTextMetrics`): each WORD is charged by the lines it takes at both prose measures (stacked 44 ems, beside the panel 28), because `wrapEms` sets a word whole and a word a line cannot share wastes the rest of it — a word just over half a line costs 2x its width. Costed in TS, on the rows read under the lock — page 4 joins every approved row into one paragraph and an overflowing page REFUSES the whole pack (`PackRefusal`). Calibrated on the tightest fixture (cost page 4 holds: wide 619, digits 620, prose 639, URL 724, CJK 799, uniform words of 10..70 chars 620-1178; up to 1766 elsewhere); 560 sits 9% under the lowest, ~1200 characters of prose. The cost takes the worse of the two layouts, so text of line-wide words is over-charged where the page is actually stacked (safe, not exact). Pinned by `packApprovedCommentaryCap.test.ts` (at budget fits 4 fixtures x 24 kinds incl. the N=10..70 word sweep and 40 seeded mixed-word texts; 3.5x refuses on all; 1.3x refuses on the tightest). Approvals are serialised per pack by `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('<company>:<kind>:<hash>', 611))` taken BEFORE the sum is read, inside the `withAuth` transaction (the service throws without one); proved against real Postgres by `tests/integration/commentary-budget-race.int.test.ts` (needs the disposable fixture DB). **Which pages the budget protects:** board pack = page 4 'Commentary and actions' (fixed sheet, budgeted). Management and monthly packs never feed approved text to a page model (only `boardPackDocument` reads it; `reports-pack.ts` uses just the draft state), they flow it on screen and in the share link, so they are NOT budgeted and take no lock; the pack type is recovered by matching `params_hash` against `canonicalParamsHash({type, period_start, period_end})`, the dates read as `to_char(.., 'YYYY-MM-DD')` so DateStyle cannot matter, and a row that matches no type is budgeted (fail closed). The share link's `<p>` breaks long words (`break-words`) and page 4's prose and derived panel have `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (`styles/packPrintTablesAndProse.css`; `anywhere`, not `break-word`, because only it lowers min-content so the `2fr 1fr` grid stops growing; proved in Chromium for prose, approver action item and panel item in both layouts by `tests/unit/print/packNarrativeLongToken.test.ts`). `fitBodyPage` (`packs/pages/packNarrativeFit.ts`) words the refusal when it is approved commentary that overflows, naming the sheet from its position. UI: `CommentaryEditor` shows 'about N characters left' (focused textarea, `role=status`, focus returns to the row on cancel/success; the Edit button is named by the sentence the row shows).
- 2026-09-26 (R-032 L5): `approveCommentary`, `rejectCommentary` now call `assertNotImpersonating()` (`src/lib/auth/impersonationGuard.ts`) as their FIRST statement: a platform-admin "Login as" session gets `ImpersonationForbiddenError` → 403 `IMPERSONATION_FORBIDDEN` before anything is read or written. Bearer callers (MCP, PATs) and jobs carry no `session_id` and pass. The guard runs one `sql` query, so a unit test that mocks `sql` with a positional queue must also mock the guard (`vi.mock('@/lib/auth/impersonationGuard', ...)` with `assertNotImpersonating: async () => undefined`) or every later query shifts by one.
- 2026-09-06: the list route's GET arm is owner/admin/manager (`canReadSharingSurface`). It returns DRAFT text, and `withWriteAccess` lets every read method through.
- 2026-09-06: migration 612 adds `withdrawn_by` / `withdrawn_at`; the replace path stamps them and leaves the approval columns intact.
- 2026-09-06: `useCommentary` no longer accepts a `sectionRef` it ignored, and a 2xx carrying the wrong envelope arm throws `ApiEnvelopeError` instead of rendering as "no commentary".
